title: Gate throughput: gate speed (F5:T7) and gate pass rate (F5:T9) to PASS
goal: Bring self-scorecard cells F5:T7 and F5:T9 to PASS without relaxing a definition and without moving any node out of the pull-request lane. Baseline over the 30 days to main 92526921 (355 counted pull_request runs): harness_performance median 710 s against a target then below 600 s, below 900 s since decision D6 (p95 1059 s, already passing), with test:cli 58% of job time because the check runner executes nodes one at a time; harness_green_main 86.8% against a target of at least 95%, with 47 failures of which 33 are real defects, 13 main-moved blocks, and 1 infrastructure (#247). Owner decisions D1 to D5 of 2026-10-07 (decisions.md): in-runner parallel workers first and sharding only if still above 600 s, auto-update branch, a pre-push preflight mandatory for agents and opt-in for humans, keep the F5:T9 definition (amended on 2026-10-08: F5:T9 measures the final-head gate outcome of each pull request), and ship 2.3.0 when both cells pass. Owner decision D6 of 2026-10-08 sets the F5:T7 PASS threshold to a median below 900 s, with p95 below 1800 s and the REVIEW bounds unchanged.

owner_effects.description: Enable the auto-update branch repository setting with the rebase update method (decision D2), after TASK-0721 records how it fits ADR-CHK-0004 and writes out the exact setting, and after TASK-0728 makes the commit-range check refuse merge commits and judge author path authority and admitted committers (ADR-CHK-0008), and provide the non-GITHUB_TOKEN credential the TASK-0726 rebase-update workflow uses. The setting alone updates no pull request; TASK-0726 is the update mechanism. OE-01 is not used: the campaign policy reserves it for a merge queue, which D2 did not choose, so serialized admission stays in force.
Publish 2.3.0 (decision D5) once harness_performance and harness_green_main both read PASS over their post-change windows, from an exact candidate under a separately authorized release.

rounds.title: Gate speed (F5:T7)
rounds.goal: The pull-request gate median falls below 900 s (decision D6 of 2026-10-08; it was 600 s) without dropping any planned node. The check runner executes independent plan nodes on a bounded worker pool under ADR-CHK-0007, with scheduling declarations in test-task-exclusivity.json and never in test-tasks.json so the package-owned verifier and release export are unaffected (T1). The job split of ADR-CHK-0007 rule 11 (T2, CTG-0713) merged in #355: on 2026-10-07 the Owner amended D1 to start it at once, without waiting for the post-merge median, because the parallel gate runs of #352 took 549 s and 798 s, too variable to rely on parallelism alone (decisions.md). test:cli runs in its own partition job, every other affected node in a second, and an aggregator keeps the single required check devai-release-gate. The check-result cache persists across CI runs keyed by task input digest with the protected-namespace recapture rule kept (T3). CTG-0717 moves the F5:T7 PASS threshold to a median below 900 s in the target record, the sensor default and its tests (T4, D6). Every task is single-role: Architect writes law and docs, Inspector tests, Engineer code. Accepted when harness_performance over the post-change window of decisions.md reads a median below 900 s and every window run accounted for its whole plan, with partitioned-out entries counted and ownership assessed across the report pair when the gate is partitioned (decisions.md).

deliverables: TGT-PERF-001 in law/targets/performance.json states a median of at most 900000 ms with threshold 900000, citing decision D6 of 2026-10-08; TGT-PERF-002 (p95 at most 1800000 ms) is unchanged.

rounds.title: Remove avoidable gate failures (F5:T9)
rounds.goal: Fewer runs fail for avoidable reasons, inside the current F5:T9 definition (D4): main-moved base-up-to-date blocks are removed only if both of these land: the auto-update branch setting with the rebase update method (T1, Owner effect OE-02), and a rebase-update trigger that rebases every open pull request when main moves, so the superseded gate run is cancelled rather than failed (T1b, TASK-0726). Real defects are caught before push by a pre-push preflight that is mandatory for agents and opt-in for humans (T2, D3), the bootstrap cache counts a hit only when every compiled file is present and otherwise rebuilds (T3, hardening after #247, already closed), and the doctor-check-result-identities flake candidate is resolved (T4). Accepted when the post-change window of decisions.md, which opens only after TASK-0726 merges and OE-02 is performed, shows no main-moved failures, real-defect failures roughly halved against 33 in 355 baseline runs, and harness_green_main at or above 95%.

packages/sensors/src/harness/reviewed-workflow-steps.ts re-reviews the digest of the changed compile step (coordinator ruling of 2026-10-08).

tasks.title: Resolve the doctor-check-result-identities flake candidate

No retry is added.

tasks.title: Prove the commit-range refusals and admitted cases for merge commits, author path authority, and committers
deliverables: Contract tests under tests/contract/ build real git ranges and prove each refusal of scripts/check-commit-range.mjs: a merge commit inside a pull-request range; an author that is not a DEVAI <Role> identity; an author role changing a path outside its Constitution Article 6 write authority; and a committer outside the admitted list (the same role as the author, the human merger of a rebase merge onto main, or the update-branch GitHub App of a rebase update).

They prove the admitted cases: a role commit committed by the same role, a rebase-merged commit committed by the human merger, and a rebase-updated commit committed by the update-branch App, each changing only paths its author role may write (ADR-CHK-0008 IA-006). The tests fail until TASK-0728 lands on the same branch.

tasks.title: Refuse merge commits and check author path authority and admitted committers in the commit range
deliverables: scripts/check-commit-range.mjs refuses any merge commit in a pull-request range.

For each commit it reads the author identity as DEVAI <Role> and refuses a commit that changes a path outside that role's Constitution Article 6 write authority, judged from the author alone (ADR-CHK-0008). It refuses a committer outside the admitted list: the same role as the author, the human merger of a rebase merge onto main, or the update-branch GitHub App of a rebase update.
Each refusal names the commit and the reason; the existing grammar and single-family checks are unchanged. TASK-0726 and Owner effect OE-02 wait for this task.

waves.title: Rebase-update trigger for open pull requests when main moves, with the repository-write effect class

tasks.title: Define the repository-write effect class, the update credential, and the update workflow page
deliverables: ADR-CHK-0008 defines the harness effect class repository-write: a step that writes repository refs or branches through the API and is not a release publication. It classifies the rebase-update step as repository-write (coordinator ruling of 2026-10-08: the rebase-update step is repository-write, not publication), and states that the update workflow uses a superseding concurrency group, so a newer push to main cancels an update run in progress. The ADR index is regenerated and law/policy/adr-validation.json is re-pinned.

law/policy/credential-requirements.json declares the update-branch GitHub App credential the update workflow consumes. .devai/config/credential-requirements-binding.json binds it for this repository, as an Architect-owned adopter binding under the ADR-CHK-0008 path table. No credential value is committed.

docs/dev/operations/workflows/update-pull-request-branches.md describes the update workflow: its trigger, the rebase update method, the expected-head guard, the App credential, the least permissions, the repository-write effect class, and the superseding concurrency.
The workflows index docs/dev/operations/workflows/README.md lists the new page, and law/policy/documentation-information-architecture.json registers it.

If the ci-economy path-filters exemption changes adopter-visible behaviour, docs/adopters/ci-economy.md states that a workflow none of whose jobs uses actions/checkout is exempt from ci-economy.path-filters.

tasks.title: Test the update workflow checker, the reviewed-step registry, and the repository-write effect class
deliverables: Contract tests mutate .github/workflows/update-pull-request-branches.yml and prove that scripts/check-workflows.mjs fails when the push-to-main trigger, the rebase update method, the expected-head-sha guard, the App credential, the least permissions, or the superseding concurrency is removed (ADR-CHK-0008 IA-005).

Tests under packages/sensors/tests/ prove that the reviewed-step registry records the rebase-update step as repository-write, and that repository-write is a harness effect class distinct from publication and read-only. A changed update step reads unknown until reviewed anew. A publication-only rule does not apply to repository-write.
Any ADR census or credential manifest counts that the TASK-07210 changes move are re-pinned. The tests fail until TASK-0726 lands on the same branch.

The live-ledger workflow fixtures include update-pull-request-branches.yml and its workflows_scanned count is re-pinned to 5. Rule cases in check-ci-economy-depth.test.ts and ci-economy-class-lane.test.ts prove that a branch-push workflow with no actions/checkout step is exempt from ci-economy.path-filters, while one that checks out the repository is still flagged.

tasks.title: Rebase every open pull request onto main when main moves, and cancel the superseded gate run
deliverables: .github/workflows/update-pull-request-branches.yml runs on push to main and, for every open non-draft pull request against main that is behind it, calls PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/update-branch with update_method rebase and the expected head sha. It skips a pull request whose rebase conflicts and reports it without failing the others. It uses a GitHub App or other non-GITHUB_TOKEN credential, because a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow run and the rebased head would never be gated. The workflow holds the least permissions it needs.

The superseded gate run is cancelled rather than failed. The existing concurrency group of pull-request-checks.yml, keyed by workflow and pull request number with cancel-in-progress, already cancels an in-progress run when the rebased head arrives as a synchronize event; the task verifies this on a live pull request, records the run ids in its pull request, and changes the gate workflow only if the verification fails.
scripts/check-workflows.mjs pins the trigger, the rebase update method, the credential source, and the concurrency group, so removing any of them fails the workflow check.

packages/sensors/src/harness/reviewed-workflow-steps.ts admits the effect class repository-write and records the reviewed rebase-update step with it, not publication (coordinator ruling of 2026-10-08: the rebase-update step is repository-write, not publication). The harness effect analysis treats repository-write as its own class, with its coherence exception in packages/sensors/src/harness-coherence.ts. .devai/config/toolchain.json declares what the update workflow needs from the toolchain.

packages/cli/src/commands/check/ci-economy.ts exempts from ci-economy.path-filters a workflow none of whose jobs uses actions/checkout. Such a workflow consumes no repository content, so path filters would save nothing, and docs:ci-economy reads PASS for update-pull-request-branches.yml.

rounds.title: F5:T9 measurement: the final-head gate outcome of each pull request (D4 amended)
rounds.goal: Redefine F5:T9 under D4 as amended on 2026-10-08: harness_green_main reads the final-head gate run of each pull request in the window, not every push, so it measures the outcome of the gate rather than developer iteration. A forward record on ADR-SCR-0010, law/policy/sensor-notes/harness_green_main.md, a sensor page under docs/theory, the sensor, and its tests carry the change. It changes what the cell means, never what the gate checks; the at-least-95% threshold is unchanged.
rounds.disposition: Opened by the Owner on 2026-10-08 ("Redefine F5:T9 now (R-0703)"), amending D4 and lifting the wait on the R-0702 window.

waves.title: Redefine the F5:T9 population as the final-head gate run of each pull request

tasks.title: Record the final-head F5:T9 population on ADR-SCR-0010, its sensor note and its sensor page
deliverables: A forward record on ADR-SCR-0010 (D4 as amended on 2026-10-08) defines the harness_green_main population as the final-head gate run of each pull request in the window: for each pull request with a gate run in the window, only the run on its final head counts. Cancelled and superseded runs stay excluded, the at-least-95% threshold is unchanged, and what the gate checks is unchanged. The catalogue is regenerated and re-pinned.

law/policy/sensor-notes/harness_green_main.md states the new population. A new sensor page docs/theory/architecture/sensors/harness_green_main.md describes how the final head of each pull request is chosen and read.

law/schemas/sensor-inputs.schema.json adds the outcomeUnit field to the harness_green_main declaration, and .devai/config/sensor-inputs.json declares outcomeUnit: pull-request-final-head for DEVAI (an Architect row in the ADR-CHK-0008 path table). A declaration that omits outcomeUnit keeps the run population of ADR-SCR-0010 (ADR-SCR-0014).

law/policy/subprocess-effects.json admits the read-only gh pr list call, and its .devai/config/subprocess-effects.json copy follows in the same commit (the law-with-generated pairing). docs/adopters/sensor-inputs.md describes the unit for adopters.

tasks.title: Test the final-head population of harness_green_main
deliverables: Tests under packages/sensors/tests/ prove that harness_green_main counts one gate run per pull request, the run on its final head. A pull request whose earlier pushes failed but whose final head passed counts green. One whose final head failed counts red. Cancelled and superseded runs are excluded. A pull request with no gate run on its final head is not counted.
The percentage, the 95% PASS and 80% REVIEW thresholds, and the reading metrics follow the per-pull-request population. The tests fail until TASK-0733 lands on the same branch.
Tests under packages/schemas/tests/ re-pin the sensor-inputs schema and its counts, including the governance-v15-adr census for ADR-SCR-0014, and prove an unknown outcomeUnit value is refused.

tasks.title: Read the final-head gate run of each pull request in harness_green_main
deliverables: packages/sensors/src/harness-green-main.ts computes its percentage over the final-head gate run of each pull request in the window. The gh-api population reader under packages/sensors/src/harness/ groups the pull_request gate runs by pull request and keeps the latest attempt of the run on each final head, through the admitted gh run list shapes.
The thresholds and the reading shape are unchanged.
packages/cli/src/authority/broker.ts classifies the new read-only gh pr list subprocess with an exact grammar (ADR-SCR-0014, ADR-SCR-0005).
